question: does the nine-cell matrix independently corroborate the measured cause of the V4.1 divergence?
the_prediction: the causal chain says the divergence needs BOTH an untrained top-k router (whose 6th-to-7th score gap falls below one BF16 epsilon on 7.2% of decisions) AND the one-fp32-ulp residual difference that flips it. A cell with no router, or with a trained router, should match its oracle despite carrying exactly the same one-ulp difference.
the_test: the nine cells were built and run for their own reasons, before this chain was measured. Splitting them by router rather than by topology is a test the matrix was not collected to answer.
result: 9 for 9. Every cell whose router is absent or trained matches; every cell whose router is untrained does not. The failing set is exactly the reduced-AND-MoE set, which is what the chain predicts and nothing else in the matrix distinguishes.
why_the_reduced_qwen3_cell_is_the_load_b: a reduced DENSE vehicle isolates the variable. It carries the same reduced widths, the same Philox weight construction, the same backends and the same one-ulp summation-order difference as the reduced V4.1 vehicles -- and it matches its oracle exactly, at [1073, 382, 93]. So reduction itself does not break a token; the untrained ROUTER does.
what_this_does_not_show: it does not prove the chain: it shows the matrix is consistent with it, using a split the matrix was not built to test
the V4-Flash rows are all SHIPPED scale, so trained-router and shipped-scale are not separated by this evidence -- a reduced V4-Flash vehicle would separate them and does not exist
not an RTL measurement: every device here is runtime.sim
